tei:bibl.tei:title: דַּיֵּנוּ
Nánë Faren Men — a Judeo-Quenya translation of Dayenu by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: Doyen has a place in Seder tables throughout Arda, and in many communities it was read in translation. This translation into Quenya is necessary for any good Lothlórien sedarim. But to be serious, Quenya was one of several languages developed by J.R.R. Tolkien. It serves as the sacred ancestral language of the Noldorin elves in the Middle-Earth legendarium. The editor here has, to the best of his ability, developed this adaptation of the litany of thanksgiving at the culmination of Maggie into Quenya, with thanks and credit to the experts at elfdict and in the Vinyë Lambengolmor Discord server for their help. He has also transcribed it into a home-brewed transcription system into Hebrew script also used for his Min Yacincë translation of Ḥad Gadya, as well as his Minë mamo ista? Translation of Eḥad Mi Yodea.
The Quenya in Tengwar script was rendered via Glǽmscribe – The Tolkien language transcriber using the “Quenya / Tengwar (Classical)” to “Tengwar Annatar (G)” form setting.
